Lesson 9 · Guided route

Audit the adjusted comparison: guided case

How much did a selected program help its eligible population?

Follow one business problem from the manager’s request to a practical next step. The short case gives the decision at a glance; the technical appendix holds the complete model and derivations.

Short caseTechnical appendix
Story chapters
  1. 01. A coaching program looks promising
  2. 02. Predict both options for the same facilities
  3. 03. Decide what evidence to buy next

Part 1 of 3

A coaching program looks promising

A service network gave process coaching to selected facilities. Coached sites average 8.57 outcome units above uncoached sites. The director wants to fund a wider rollout, but the facilities were chosen partly because of their starting conditions. The director needs the gain coaching would produce for a defined set of eligible facilities, not the difference between two existing lists.

Before fitting a model, the analyst writes down the trial they would have preferred: eligibility, coaching start date, comparison facilities, outcome window, and what counts as the coaching package. That design note prevents later choices from being made only because they yield an attractive result.

The trial note should be written with operations staff, not just analysts. They know whether “coaching” meant the same activities at every facility, when staff first learned they were selected, and whether another initiative arrived at the same time. Those facts determine the intervention being evaluated and the start of follow-up long before a modeling choice matters.

Part 2 of 3

Predict both options for the same facilities

The analyst uses pre-coaching characteristics to predict each facility’s outcome under coaching and under no coaching, then averages the predicted differences over the target population. In this generated case, that standardized estimate is 3.86 units. It is more relevant to the rollout question than the raw 8.57-unit gap.

From a group gap to a defined rollout target
ComparisonOutcome units
Raw coached–uncoached gap8.57
Standardized all-facility estimate3.86

This comparison is credible only where facilities had a real chance of being in either group. A model cannot create an uncoached counterpart for a type of facility that always received coaching. The analysis therefore shows overlap and checks whether a few unusual facilities carry too much weight.

Standardization asks the model two questions for each facility: what outcome is predicted with coaching, and what is predicted without it? The difference is then averaged over the facilities in the proposed rollout. This makes the target tangible. It also makes missing comparison types visible: if no uncoached facility resembles a particular coached site, its second prediction rests mainly on extrapolation.

Part 3 of 3

Decide what evidence to buy next

The director can compare the estimated gain with the cost of coaches, staff time, and disruption, while reserving resources for a stronger follow-up. A limited rollout with a recorded assignment rule would be more informative than another round of retrospective adjustment.

The memo should distinguish two questions: whether coaching helped facilities like those already coached, and whether it would help every eligible facility. Different target mixes produce different answers when effects vary. The practical recommendation should name which population the budget actually covers.

The budget memo can show an estimated benefit per facility beside coaching cost and the number of sites with credible comparisons. A second phase could deliberately assign coaching among sites where the decision remains uncertain. That is a better use of scarce evaluation resources than polishing an adjusted estimate for facilities that never had a realistic alternative in the historical data.

Decision check

Why is the adjusted all-facility estimate a better starting point for network-wide expansion than the raw group gap?

Compare your reasoning

It compares predicted coached and uncoached outcomes for the same target mix, instead of comparing groups selected under different starting conditions.

Compare with the known truth

Reveal the generator truth

The generated average effect is 3.87. The script can reveal it because it created both potential outcomes; an actual program evaluation cannot observe that truth directly.

This comparison is possible because the case is synthetic. The full generating process is in the appendix.
